text:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing a cluster of NVIDIA Xid 79s from ap-northeast1 on A10 machines since ~03:00UTC. Mostly on embedder pods, small batches (1-8) but high qps. any quick thoughts? :rotating_light:

maria: can you paste the mem/dmesg snippet? is it ECC or decode-related?

ops-bot: Alert: gpu_error_count[ap-northeast1_a10] spiked from 2/hr -> 45/hr at 2025-11-12T03:05:12Z (inc: Xid79).

alex: log tail from one host below:
```
[  103.456789] NVRM: Xid (79): 31 0x50d9c2f3 0x0 0x0
[  103.456792] NVRM: GPU 0: A10-1 tripped Xid 79
[  103.456795] kernel: compute-task: panic decode error
```

saugat: quick hypothesis: Xid79 often shows as ECC/PCIe decode noise on A10s in our fleet. but correlation with tiny-batch embedder is interesting — could be bursty memory traffic pattern exposing a flaky card. ran a query across errors by tenant/optype:
```
SELECT tenant, optype, COUNT(*) as errs
FROM gpu_error_events
WHERE xid = 79 AND region = 'ap-northeast1' AND date >= '2025-11-10'
GROUP BY tenant, optype
ORDER BY errs DESC
LIMIT 20;
-- results (sample):
# tenantA, embedder, 128
# tenantB, chat-encoder, 12
# tenantC, embedder, 9
```

maria: nice. do we have batchshape breakdown? small batches will increase PCIe transactions/keystate churn.

saugat: grabbed batchshape histogram for tenantA (last 48h):
```
batch_size: 1 -> 54%
batch_size: 2-4 -> 32%
batch_size: 5-8 -> 10%
batch_size: >8 -> 4%
```
This tenant pushes a lot of tiny 1-2 token inference requests (edge embedder).

linh: also saw network drops on that rack around same time. NIC counters show link flaps on eth0-1 at 03:04UTC. could be coupled: transient PCIe + link glitch -> Xid 79. attaching NIC snippet: "rx_errors: 12, tx_errors: 10, link_flaps: 3"

alex: ops-bot, can you surface recent soft-drain history for that host? want to see if this card has been moved previously.

ops-bot: softdrain history for host gpu-a10-az1-17:
- 2025-10-28: softdrain auto for eviction (thermal), cleared after 12h
- 2025-11-05: manual maintenance, nvlink reseat
- 2025-11-12 02:58: automatic requeue triggered by Xid79 threshold

derek: Given the recurrence and tenant hotspot, propose immediate mitigations:
- set routing rule to steer tenantA embedder traffic off this rack -> route to eu-west warm pool (lower latency impact than full outage)
- bump small-batch coalescing on runtime for tenantA (window 50ms) to reduce tiny-batch frequency
- drain GPU 0 on gpu-a10-az1-17 for hardware replacement if errors persist after routing

maria: agree on mitigations. add cost note: steering to warm pool increases cross-region egress + higher p95 latency; estimate $0.06/1k requests extra for tenantA while routed. also longer coalescing may increase tail latency for single-request flows.

alex: we tested increasing prefix caching and batching in staging; embed quality unaffected for tenantA on 50ms coalesce. I'll flip routing rule now and open a hardware ticket if errors > 5 in next hour.

saugat: one more data point — Xid distribution across op types in the cluster (last 7d):
```
Xid13: lookups/kv ops  -> 24% (mostly large-batch decode)
Xid31: occasional ECC/thermal -> 12%
Xid48: mixed driver resets -> 8%
Xid79: dominant for tiny-batch embedder -> 56%
```
suggests Xid79 is workload-sensitive while others are more general.

linh: I'll keep NIC team posted; they will rack-swap the cable and validate SFPs. if link flaps stop but Xid persists, escalate hardware.

alex: routing rule pushed: tenantA embedder -> warm-eu-west pool (enabled 03:22UTC). monitoring. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Route change applied. previous sessions draining gracefully.

maria: status check in 30m. if error rate drops 80% we mark as workload-driven and file playbook to tune coalescing + batching defaults for high-small-batch tenants.

derek: created hw ticket #HW-2025-847 to RMA GPU if post-routing errors > 5/hr. attaching host logs and NIC counters.

alex: thanks all. summary for postmortem: probable flaky A10 showing Xid79 under tiny-batch embedder load, NIC flaps may have amplified. mitigation = routing + coalescing; next step RMA if persists.

maria: closing note — we should add an automated detection rule: when Xid79 correlates >60% with batch_size <=2 for a host, auto-redirect tenant traffic and alert infra-oncall. low false-positive risk.

saugat: I'll prototype the metric + alert (count(xid79 & batch<=2)/count(xid79) > 0.6) and share the query.

linh: thanks — will validate NIC health checks in rack-level runbook.
